## Judgment

### Expected-drift set

sweet16, petunia, groot@forge — the three configs where
`programs.dev-home.enableLlmAgents` is true and the Claude integration is
therefore active. avina and hermes never declare the option; dualie sets it
false. Those three must show no drift, and the gate is the only thing
holding that, so it is the real assertion of this change.

### Actual vs expected

Match, including the negative half: avina, hermes and groot@dualie are
byte-identical drv paths to the previous baseline. `groot@rk3588` N/A on
this arch as usual.

Content of the drift on sweet16/ddukes: one entry added to `home.file`,
`.claude/hooks/herdr-agent-state.sh`. No package change — `home.packages`
diffs empty between the two revs. The symlink target is the existing
`herdr-claude-hook-0.7.5` derivation already in the closure, so nothing new
is built or fetched; this is a pure file-tree addition.

### Why the raw script and not the wrapper

Established by testing the 0.7.5 binary directly, against four states of
the canonical path:

  absent                        -> "not installed"
  arbitrary script, no marker   -> "outdated (legacy < v7)"
  symlink -> raw script         -> "current (v7)"
  symlink -> wrapper            -> "outdated (legacy < v7)"

herdr parses `HERDR_INTEGRATION_VERSION` out of that file. The wrapper is a
generated bash shim and carries no marker, so it reports as legacy. The raw
script is therefore what the canonical path points at, while settings.json
continues to invoke the wrapper — same script body, but with python3 and
coreutils pinned onto PATH.

### Clobber risk checked before deploying

Home Manager refuses to overwrite an unmanaged file. `ls` on both affected
hosts confirmed nothing exists at `~/.claude/hooks/herdr-agent-state.sh`.
The other hooks in that directory (session-start.sh, langfuse_hook.py,
context-mode-cache-heal.mjs, notify-mailgun.sh) are hand-authored and stay
that way — only this one path becomes Nix-managed.

### Consequence worth recording

`herdr integration install claude` and `herdr integration uninstall claude`
will now fail on these hosts: the path is a read-only store symlink. That
is intended. A herdr version bump moves the symlink and the reported
version follows it, which is the behaviour the imperative installer was
providing before.
